extracted.intended_audience: indexers, book editors, and publishing production staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, editing, formatting, and submitting indexes for books and similar publications, including deciding headings/subheadings, locators, alphabetizing, typographic conventions, and index submission and typesetting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index length and inclusiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Fifteen or more will yield a fairly long index (about one-twentieth the length of the text or more). If the publisher has budgeted for a strictly limited number of pages, the indexer should work accordingly. Remember that it is always easier to drop entries than to add them; err on the side of inclusiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If space is limited, tailor the index to publisher limits; otherwise be inclusive—it's easier to remove entries than add them later. See related sections for trimming and publisher specs.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to mark entries on proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark principal headings and subheadings clearly on proofs (a colon separates proposed principal heading from subheading). Invert personal names for headings (Perry, Bliss), mark plurals where appropriate, supply first names in the margin if needed, and mark titles and other terms as they appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Underline or otherwise mark headings, subheads, names, titles, and proposed modifications on page proofs so they can be transcribed into index entries; use margin notes for first names or disambiguation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan and include subentry modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: For each term marked, make an effort to write in a modification—a word or phrase that narrows the application of the heading, hence a potential subentry. Although some such modifications may eventually be dropped, they should be kept on hand in case they are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications prevent main headings from becoming long strings of locators and can be altered or added as indexing proceeds. Keep provisional subheads while indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record inclusive locators for extended discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a text discussion extends over more than one page, section, or paragraph, both beginning and ending numbers—which will depend on what locator system is being used—must be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inclusive page or paragraph ranges for continuous discussions (e.g., 54-56) and follow the project's locator conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical entry elements while typing
rubrics_metrics.description: Most entries at this stage will include three elements: a heading, a modification (or provisional subentry), and a locator (page or paragraph number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While typing, you will probably modify headings, add/delete/alter subheadings and locators, and update cross-references and alphabetical order. After typing each entry, read it carefully against the page proofs to check locators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetizing system choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to use the letter-by-letter or the word-by-word system. Many indexers alphabetize as they type; others let their software do it, intervening as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the chosen system proves unsatisfactory for the particular work as the index proceeds, a switch can be made if the publisher agrees. See referenced sections for details on letter-by-letter vs word-by-word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final check for omissions against proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: After typing all the entries, read quickly through the marked-up proofs once again to see whether anything indexable has been omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late developments in later chapters may make previously peripheral items significant; remedy omissions at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and report typographical errors found while indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Although not engaged to proofread, the indexer usually finds typographical errors and minor inconsistencies. If indexing a book, keep track of all such errors and send a list to the publisher when, or before, submitting the index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a list of errors found and provide it to the publisher with the index submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refine main heading terms and prepare cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit assembled entries to a coherent whole. Choose among synonymous or closely related terms and, if necessary, prepare suitable cross-references to reflect those choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For journals, retain terms established in previous volumes. Prepare cross-references that reflect chosen terminology and aid finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide main entries versus subentries by likely lookup behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether certain items are best treated as main entries or as subentries under another heading. Consider where readers will look first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote subentries to main entries when readers would search for them directly; avoid indexes with few main entries but masses of subentries, which are unhelpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide subentries when locators exceed five or six
rubrics_metrics.description: Main headings unmodified by subentries should not be followed by more than five or six locators. If a draft index shows long strings of locators, it should be broken up into a number of subentries to lead readers quickly to information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking long locator lists into subentries improves usability; the extra space is worth reader convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phrase subheadings concisely and begin with likely keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Subheadings should be as concise and informative as possible and begin with a keyword likely to be sought. A, an, and the are omitted whenever possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rambling subheadings; prefer compact, searchable phrases. Use defined/dedicated subheads (e.g., 'defined') for undifferentiated locators when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check cross-references after editing headings
rubrics_metrics.description: As a final or near-final step, make sure that all cross-references match the edited headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure cross-references are needed and consistent in placement within entries; substitute locators for 'see' refs when only a few locators are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index submission formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the publisher requires a printout, allow margins of at least one inch both left and right, and leave the text unjustified. Do not format the index in columns. Use hard returns only at the end of each entry and, for an indented-style index, at the end of each subentry. Use single line spacing, and apply hanging indents using your software’s indentation feature. Do not impose end-of-line hyphenation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple indexes exist, give each an appropriate title (Author Index, Subject Index, etc.) and save each in a separate file. Keep a copy of the final draft and marked-up proofs until publication; send publisher a list of errors found.

rubrics_metrics.name: If an index is irreparably bad, omit or replace it
rubrics_metrics.description: As an editor, you cannot remake a really bad index. If an index cannot be repaired, you have two choices: omit it or have a new one made by another indexer (at additional cost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess repairability early and advise publisher on costs and options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check headings for alphabetical order (index-editing checklist #1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check headings—in both the main entries and subentries—for alphabetical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the entire index follows the chosen alphabetizing system consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check spelling, capitalization, and font for each heading (checklist #2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the spelling, capitalization, and font (i.e., italics or roman) of each heading, consulting the page proofs if in doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify style and typography against the work and style conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check punctuation for style and consistency (checklist #3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check punctuation—commas, colons, semicolons, en dashes, etc.—for proper style and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the manual's punctuation style rules for indexes; ensure uniform usage throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check cross-references lead to matching headings (checklist #4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check cross-references to make sure they go somewhere and that headings match. Make sure they are needed; if only a few locators are involved, substitute these for the see reference. Ensure that placement of cross-references within entries is consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test each see/see also reference; convert unnecessary cross-refs to direct locators when concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add cross-references you believe are necessary (checklist #5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add cross-references you believe are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert see/see also references to aid discoverability where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect and correct false locators and ensure ascending order (checklist #6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check to make sure there are no false locators such as “193-93” or “12102” (and figure out whether these may be the product of a typo) and make sure the locators to each main heading and subheading are in ascending order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag typographical locator errors and confirm correct ranges and sequencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check subentries for consistent ordering (checklist #7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check subentries for consistency of order, whether alphabetical or chronological.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the chosen ordering method uniformly to subentries to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine overanalyzed single-locator subentries where possible (checklist #8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If some entries seem overanalyzed (many subentries with only one locator or with the same locator), try to combine some of them if it can be done without sacrificing their usefulness. If subheadings are more elaborately worded than necessary, try to simplify them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance granularity and usability; simplify verbose subheads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct awkward or unnecessary sub-subentries (checklist #9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If awkward or unnecessary sub-subentries appear, correct them by adding appropriate repeated subentries or by adjusting punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid deeply nested sub-subentries when a simpler structure will do; use repetition or punctuation adjustments to clarify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break up long strings of unanalyzed locators (checklist #10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for long strings of unanalyzed locators and break them up, if possible, with subentries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace long lists of pages with focused subentries to improve scannability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random-check locators for accuracy (checklist #11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the accuracy of locators by a random check of five to ten entries. If more than one error shows up, consult the author or the indexer; every locator may have to be rechecked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use random sampling to assess overall locator reliability; escalate if multiple errors are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trim trivial entries cautiously (checklist #12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the index needs trimming, delete any entries (and cross-references thereto) that you know from your work on the book are trivial, such as references to persons or places used only as examples. But be careful. You may offend someone or let yourself in for a lot of work. A handful of unnecessary entries, if they are very short, will not mar an otherwise good index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When trimming, balance completeness and publishing constraints; consult editors/authors when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typesetting specification note for index manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief typesetting note after consulting publisher specs (example: Set two columns, flush and hang, ragged right; indent subentries one em; indent runovers two ems; preserve en dashes between continuing numbers; leave one line space between alphabetical blocks. Set headnote across both columns.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a typesetter's instruction note to avoid misinterpretation; tailor to publisher's detailed design specs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type size and column width guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexes are usually set in smaller type than the body—often two sizes smaller. Indexes are usually set in two columns (e.g., with a 27-pica page the columns might be 13 picas each with a one-pica gutter); large-format works may use three or four columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow publisher's design specifications for point size and column count; this impacts indentation and runover rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set indexes ragged right (do not justify)
rubrics_metrics.description: For very short lines, justifying the text usually results in gaping word spaces or excessive hyphenation; therefore set all indexes without justification (ragged right).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ragged-right setting to improve readability of short index lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation depths for entries and runovers
rubrics_metrics.description: All runover lines are indented, whether subentries are run in or indented. In an indented index the subentries may be indented one em, the sub-subentries two ems, and the runovers for all entries three ems. Decide these depths before type is set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine indentation scheme in advance and apply consistently; runovers should be indented more deeply than subentries for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix bad column breaks and single-line orphans
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid leaving a line consisting of only one or two page numbers at the top of a column or a single line at the end or beginning of an alphabetic section. Eliminate such blemishes by rebreaking entries, transposing lines between columns, adding white space, or adjusting column lengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review typeset index for columnation problems and correct by rebreaking or transposition to avoid orphans and widows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'continued' lines for entries carried across pages
rubrics_metrics.description: If an entry breaks at the foot of the last column on a right-hand page and resumes at the top of the following left-hand page, the main heading should be repeated, followed by the word continued in parentheses, above the carried-over part of the index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat the main heading with '(continued)' to orient readers when entries carry across a recto–verso break.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ typographic distinctions with a headnote key
rubrics_metrics.description: A complicated index can be easier to read by using different type styles or fonts (e.g., set writers' names in caps/small caps, italicize page references to illustrations, use boldface for principal treatment). If such devices are used, a headnote to the index must furnish a key.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear headnote explaining any typographic coding used in the index (italics, bold, caps, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deep nesting; prefer run-in sub-subentries if essential
rubrics_metrics.description: If occasional sub-subentries are required they may be used, but sub-sub-subentries should be avoided if at all possible; if essential, they must be run in to the sub-subentries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult publisher before proceeding with many sub-subentries; prefer shallower structures for usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use typographic conventions for special page references (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Page numbers in italics may be used to refer to figures and tables; boldface page numbers can indicate definitions. If such conventions are used, explain them in a headnote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt consistent conventions (italic for figures, bold for definitions) and document them in the index headnote.

rubrics_metrics.name: If many sub-subentries are likely, check with publisher
rubrics_metrics.description: If it looks as though an index is going to require a great many sub-subentries, the indexer should check with the publisher before proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm space and design allowances with the publisher when deep subdivision is anticipated to avoid typesetting or budgetary problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and file separation for multiple indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is more than one index, give each an appropriate title (Author Index, Subject Index, etc.) and save each in a separate file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label and submit multiple indexes separately to facilitate typesetting and review.
